title: Medical plans
summary: Overview of UnitedHealthcare employer medical plans, including network strategy, Centers of Excellence, payment integrity, the Premium program and the range of plan options.

atoms.title: How UnitedHealthcare medical plans are built
atoms.question: What is UnitedHealthcare's approach to employer medical plans?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare medical plans are built with tailored network strategies and innovative benefit and plan designs to help meet the care and cost needs of employers and their employees. Plan designs are built for access, supported by the nation's largest proprietary network, and designed to guide employees to evidence-based, cost-efficient care.
questions: What makes UnitedHealthcare employer medical plans different?
Does UnitedHealthcare have a large proprietary network?

atoms.title: Plan designs that encourage health ownership
atoms.question: How do UnitedHealthcare plan designs encourage healthier choices?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare plan designs and popular benefits, such as $0 copays and virtual care access, are built to help promote healthier choices and encourage employees to take steps toward better health. Plans also include tools and resources to help employees understand their plan and navigate the health care system to get care at the right place, at the right time.
questions: Do UnitedHealthcare plans offer $0 copays?
What tools help employees understand their health plan?

atoms.title: Provider collaboration and Naviguard
atoms.question: How does UnitedHealthcare work with providers to control costs?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare works with providers through incentives, value-based arrangements and collaborative data sharing to help enable quality, cost-efficient care. Tools and resources like Naviguard aim to protect all parties from egregious billing, to ensure providers are paid quickly for their services and to keep out-of-network charges in check for members.
questions: What is Naviguard?
How does UnitedHealthcare keep out-of-network charges down?

atoms.title: Centers of Excellence shorten transplant stays
atoms.question: What results does UnitedHealthcare report for its Centers of Excellence program?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare's Centers of Excellence (COE) program is designed to drive lower costs, fewer complications and shorter recovery times. As an example, the page cites a 22% shorter length of hospital stay for transplant patients compared to the national benchmark, based on a Milliman transplant cost estimate and an Optum book-of-business comparison.
questions: What are Centers of Excellence in health insurance?
How much shorter are hospital stays at Centers of Excellence?

atoms.title: Payment integrity and wasteful spending
atoms.question: How much health care spending is wasteful, and what does payment integrity save?
atoms.text: Experts estimate that 25% of all health care spending is wasteful, according to a 2019 JAMA study cited by UnitedHealthcare. Its payment integrity solutions use strategies such as focused claims reviews to help identify errors and fraud or abuse, which the page says has resulted in $34.86 average savings per member per month (2018 UnitedHealthcare ASO data).
questions: What is payment integrity in health insurance?
How much can payment integrity save per member per month?

atoms.title: Primary care engagement and lower costs
atoms.question: How does primary care engagement affect health care costs?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare cites National Health Expenditures data showing that patients who regularly engaged with a primary care provider (PCP) had 10% lower costs than those who did not, and that PCPs can impact 62% of the health care dollar. UnitedHealthcare works with providers on site of care guidance, reducing unnecessary or duplicative testing and cost-effective prescribing.

How much of the health care dollar do PCPs influence?

atoms.title: Range of UnitedHealthcare medical plan options
atoms.question: Which medical plan options does UnitedHealthcare offer employers?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare lists a selection of medical plan options: Choice and Choice Plus; UnitedHealthcare Navigate and UnitedHealthcare Charter; Surest; Tiered benefits; NexusACO; UnitedHealthcare FlexWork; UnitedHealthcare Level Funded and All Savers Alternate Funding; a Preventive Plan; and International benefits. Options range from broad open access networks to more focused access.

atoms.title: Flexible features in many medical plans
atoms.question: Can UnitedHealthcare medical plans include out-of-network coverage?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare's medical plan placemat shows options ranging from broad open access networks to more focused access. Many plans have flexible design features that allow for out-of-network coverage and additional savings opportunities for employers and employees. Brokers can use the portfolio tool to design benefit packages for their clients.

atoms.title: Level Funded and All Savers Alternate Funding
atoms.question: What are Level Funded and All Savers Alternate Funding plans?
atoms.text: UnitedHealthcare Level Funded and All Savers Alternate Funding plans are designed for more flexibility and simplicity. Because they are based on participants' actual medical claims, plans may get a surplus refund at year-end if claims are lower than expected. Benefits include more savings (exemption from many ACA regulations and state premium taxes), more stability (fixed monthly costs and safeguards against high claims) and more flexibility (plan designs, wellness programs and telemedicine at no additional cost).

atoms.title: UnitedHealth Premium designation program
atoms.question: What is the UnitedHealth Premium program?
atoms.text: The UnitedHealth Premium designation program uses evidence-based measures to prioritize high-performing providers. Providers earn blue hearts for consistent delivery of quality care, and only then are they measured on their ability to manage costs efficiently. Designations appear in UnitedHealthcare online physician directories at myuhc.com, are for informational purposes only and should not be the sole basis for choosing a physician.

How does UnitedHealthcare choose Premium providers?

atoms.title: Open access network size
atoms.question: How large is UnitedHealthcare's open-access national network?
atoms.text: A UnitedHealthcare open-access plan featured on the medical plans page offers a large national network with more than 1 million doctors and over 6,000 hospitals, based on UnitedHealthcare Employer & Individual network statistics ending Q2 2020. The page presents this alongside a flier on UnitedHealthcare Choice Plus.
